method: Live @oai/sky physical input, one input followed by refreshed native screenshot. Significant visible LCD frames independently transcribed; implementation golden assertions are not independent oracle measurements. Pinned manual section 14 and guide supplied locally supplement the live observations.
observations: 2 then 2nd HEX displays 2-to-HEX, lower 2 and H marker.
Direct keys pi and ln enter A and F without ALPHA; A+F evaluates to HEX 19.
Converting displayed HEX 19 gives BIN 11001; invalid digit 2 is ignored.
ON/C clears entry while retaining BIN; HOME returns to NORMAL decimal.
Sign key inserts prefix NEG; 1NEG followed by ENT reports upper Error 1 and blank lower; NEG1 gives binary 1111111111.
Negative one converts to HEX FFFFFFFFFF, PEN 4444444444, OCT 7777777777, then decimal -1. Native visible upper viewport scrolls on these conversions.
1OR1AND0 in BIN gives 1; AND precedes OR.
HEX 3 divided by 2 multiplied by 2 gives 2, proving intermediate truncation.
Decimal 512 to BIN reports upper Error 2, blank lower, and no nondecimal marker; failed conversion leaves decimal selected.
BIN 1XNOR0 evaluates to 1111111110 (-2); BIN 1XOR1 evaluates to 0.
manualPolicy: Five-base conversions, basic four operations, parentheses, and memories are available. Nondecimal fractions cannot be entered; fractional decimal conversions and nondecimal divisions truncate.
AND, OR, XOR, XNOR, NOT, NEG are nondecimal operations.
Hexadecimal digits use direct A-F keys; B and D render b and d.
Saved equation recall containing unavailable functions or digits reports Error 5.
limitations: Ten-digit radix-complement ranges follow the observed negative-one words; exact positive and negative boundary cases are covered by integer tests, with native measured conversion boundary recorded separately.
Long native LCD source viewports are transcribed as visible and retained as raw-state known differences; web display scrolls rather than reproducing native pixel clipping.
Unmeasured native editor cursor/blink timing, deep pending-buffer transitions and all pental bitwise corner cases do not constitute full native parity.
Formula and memory regression coverage supplements pinned manual policy; every base/store pair was not individually measured in this native run.
